patch_resolves_note: The fixed original resolves the reproduced 6-byte crash by returning at the FILE_REGEX guard before any window or memchr state is derived from `offset = 12`. The adjacent `size13_append7_zeros` perturbation is used only to witness the guarded root obligation with the protected memchr event present; that witness later trips a separate allocator failure after the verified sink event executes.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project read on the observed path. In the top-level fonts rule `magic/Magdir/fonts:153`, `mcopy` materializes the exact 6-byte witness into `ms->ms_value` so libmagic can compare the sfnt signature and route into the `sfnt-font` named rule.

Root cause. The FILE_REGEX precondition rejects only a NULL source pointer; it does not reject `nbytes < offset`. That lets the `sfnt-font` regex continuation run with `offset = 12` on a 6-byte buffer.

MSan crash site. The FILE_REGEX newline scan runs `memchr` over the out-of-range search window `[s + 12, s + 332)`, so it reads uninitialized bytes from unrelated heap memory instead of from the 6-byte witness.
At regex window setup, `buf = s + offset` starts beyond the logical end of the 6-byte witness, so the later scan begins outside the live input.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original assertion trace records `regex_window.window_start_ptr > regex_window.input_end_ptr`.

edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `regex_guard.offset == regex_window.offset == 12`; the fixed `size13_append7_zeros` witness preserves the same equality.
Both the vulnerable original and the fixed `size13_append7_zeros` witness record `regex_window.window_start_ptr == regex_memchr_sink.scan_start_ptr`.
